content.text: Section 11 fully addresses this rule, and § 16.5 confirms Customer Data is governed by it rather than the general return/destroy provision.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets or exceeds our preferred position. Section 11.1 gives us up to six months' transition assistance on request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form (better than Vendor's then-current rates) and including knowledge transfer, replacement-supplier cooperation and continued service at existing scope and service levels. Section 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and bars withholding data over a fee dispute. Section 11.3 requires secure deletion (active systems and backups as they cycle, with only a legally required copy retained, which stays protected and use-restricted) plus written officer certification. Section 10.1's access cut-off runs only "after any agreed transition period" and expressly preserves Customer Data rights, and Section 16.5 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15, so the general confidentiality return/destroy provision does not undercut the exit rights. No redline needed.
